It parses the real prompt and asserts all eight bound values — plan digest, role, origin, HTTP method, canonical path, manifest digest, falconBuild id and approvals root real path — types the generated challenge exactly once through the pty, asserts exit 0 and exactly one verifying ledger entry, then asserts that replay yields APPROVAL_REQUIRED exit 14 and that each of the eight single-field binding substitutions yields exit 14, removes all approval state in teardown, and asserts the real run/ and data/ digest sets are byte-identical. A source scan asserts that no CLI flag, environment key, config key or file supplies the challenge or bypasses the interaction, consistent with OWNER-09. The test is local and manual only, because AC-084 fails on any approve flag reachable from a workflow; CI runs only the deterministic negative half — piped stdio, CI set, a wrong challenge and the in-process require refusal — and the AC-084 walker. Documentation states that it proves the production interaction path and does not authorise CI to approve real customer actions. Each assertion has a named inversion: removing the isatty gate, accepting a challenge from argv or environment, generating the challenge before rendering the prompt, omitting any bound prompt line, dropping the consumption marker, relaxing one binding field or dropping the environment allowlist must each make the test fail.. The pty helper cannot run in CI by structure, and environment detection is defence in depth only and never the primary control, consistent with OWNER-09. The helper and its test exist at exactly one path under tests/pilot/manual/, which no testMatch, testDir, npm script or workflow line reachable from .github/workflows/ci.yml resolves and which is excluded from the published package; the AC-084 walker fails the CI build on any transitive require, dynamic require, import, spawn or exec argument, npm, yarn or npx script or workflow run line from any workflow that reaches that directory or the string pty-approve; the helper refuses any approvals root or audit root whose real path is not under a directory it created itself in this process beneath the real path of os.tmpdir(), and refuses any path inside the repository, run/ or data/; and as defence in depth its first executable statement, before it builds the child environment allowlist and therefore before CI and GITHUB_ variables are stripped, throws pty_helper_refused_in_ci if its own environment has any of CI, GITHUB_ACTIONS, GITHUB_RUN_ID, GITHUB_WORKFLOW, CONTINUOUS_INTEGRATION, BUILD_ID or TF_BUILD set. A deterministic CI case asserts that requiring the helper with CI set throws, and that case is explicitly not the justification for the environment check being sufficient. Inversions: moving the helper to a CI-reachable path, or naming it in a workflow run line, must each fail the AC-084 walker; pointing it at the repository approvals root must be refused; removing the first-statement check must fail the CI case.

criteria.requirement: Every JavaScript intrinsic and built-in method on which a pilot approval, gate, fixture or filesystem decision depends is captured once at module load in uncurried form, bound through a Function.prototype.call reference taken before any other code in the module runs, and is thereafter invoked only by direct call, never through a live .call, .apply or .bind property lookup and never through the global Reflect.apply. The captured set is at least WeakSet.prototype.add and has, WeakMap.prototype.get, set and has, the net.Server.prototype address method and listening getter, EventEmitter.prototype.listeners and listenerCount, Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty, crypto.timingSafeEqual and every fs.promises method used on a pilot hot path. A load-time assertion that each captured value is typeof function fails closed with PILOT_INTERNAL_ERROR exit 18, intrinsic_capture_failed. A runtime case, labelled in the suite as a smoke check for misconfiguration and careless tampering and never as an integrity control, asserts for each capture that uncurry(Function.prototype.toString) applied to it reports native code, that its own property names are exactly length and name, and that inspecting it with hidden properties at depth four does not reveal the bound receiver. A runtime case replaces Function.prototype.call, Function.prototype.apply, Function.prototype.bind, the global Reflect.apply, WeakSet.prototype.add and WeakSet.prototype.has after module load, each alone and all together, and pollutes Object.prototype, Array.prototype and Function.prototype, and asserts that the ledger predicate's verdict is unchanged, that no value passed to any replacement is a WeakSet or a registry, that no forged object can be registered, and that the replacements record zero invocations; the inversion is that reverting any one capture to the dotted call form must make this case fail. A further case, marked in the suite as a documented limitation and never as a passing control, replaces WeakSet.prototype.add and has before the module loads and asserts the documented outcome that a forged approval is then accepted, so that the pre-load scope statement cannot silently drift. A static check asserts that no file under src/core/pilot/approval/ or src/core/pilot/PilotActionGate.js contains the substrings .call(, .apply(, .bind( or Reflect.apply( other than the single uncurry definition line, and that the capture block is the first executable statement group after "use strict". The architecture claims no integrity property for this check: a genuine uncurried capture is itself a bound function, so it stringifies as native code and has own property names exactly length and name, and a behaviour-preserving bound wrapper planted before module load is indistinguishable from it on every one of those signals, the only observed difference being the own name property, which is configurable on a bound function and therefore attacker-settable. The load-time assertion fails loudly only for a careless pre-load tamper that leaves a captured value non-callable; a behaviour-preserving pre-load tamper does not fail at all and a forged approval is then accepted, and the documented-limitation case covers both the WeakSet-replacement variant and the pre-load Function.prototype.bind bound-wrapper variant.

criteria.requirement: No protected request whose target origin differs from the page's top-level origin and the approved origin is ever routed, performed, continued, fulfilled or emulated by Falcon in Phase 18. The origin-equality gate is evaluated before the route is armed and before any request is issued, from the page's top-level origin, the origin recorded in the consumed approval and the origin of the hop-zero request URL, each computed with the WHATWG URL parser and compared as a serialized origin by string equality; inequality, an opaque origin and a non-fetchable scheme are each POLICY_PROTECTED_CROSS_ORIGIN_UNSUPPORTED exit 18 with the three origins audited. A manifest declaring a cross-origin protected route is refused at manifest load with the same reason. A runtime case places the page on one loopback origin and the protected POST target on a second loopback origin whose server answers the CORS preflight with 403, with a custom CSRF header, a JSON body, a SameSite Lax cookie on the target and serviceWorkers set to block, and asserts refusal before arming and zero transmissions at the target server, neither an OPTIONS nor a POST; the inversion removes the origin-equality check and the case must then record a POST, which is the reviewer's measured result. A second runtime case asserts the same-origin path still performs exactly one transmission with no landing hop and audits three equal origins. A third asserts that a top-level origin change between arming and dispatch is POLICY_PROTECTED_ORIGIN_CHANGED exit 18 and that the record does not claim the hop was prevented. A unit table covers uppercase hosts, present and omitted default ports, a trailing host dot, userinfo, IDNA and punycode pairs, http against https on one host, sibling subdomains, about blank, blob, data, file and null, and its inversion replaces the comparison with host-suffix or same-site matching so that the sibling-subdomain and scheme rows must fail. The equality required is between four origins, the initiator's, the page's top-level document's, the approved one and the hop-zero target's, and not between the last three alone; the rev 14 formulation keyed on the top-level origin is corrected, because a cross-origin iframe initiating a protected POST back to the top-level origin satisfied it and the request was transmitted with a cookie the browser withheld under SameSite while the frame read a response CORS would have blocked. A runtime case places a cross-origin iframe on the page, has the frame initiate the protected POST to the top-level origin with the target answering the CORS preflight 403, and asserts refusal before arming with the initiator origin named in the audit entry and zero POSTs at the target; its inversion restores the top-level-only gate and must then record a POST carrying the withheld cookie. A further case covers a nested chain whose outer and inner frames share the top-level origin but whose middle frame does not, and asserts refusal. A third asserts that a worker-initiated or service-worker-initiated protected request is refused with POLICY_PROTECTED_INITIATOR_UNSUPPORTED exit 18 and that the audit entry records why the initiator could not be established. In the origin-comparison unit table every row states its expected verdict explicitly: IDN and punycode spellings of one host, uppercase hosts, present and omitted default ports, and alternative numeric forms of one address each compare equal and arm, while sibling subdomains, differing schemes, differing ports, a trailing host dot, userinfo and the opaque and non-fetchable schemes each refuse, with the blob row refused by the scheme-first screen and a further inversion that reorders the screen so the blob row must fail. DEFERRED under owner decision OWNER-12 (Option C): no protected non-GET request reaches arming in Phase 18, so this gate has no Phase 18 trigger. The criterion is retained unweakened as an entry requirement of 18P-PROTECTED-NONGET. Its refusal obligations are subsumed by AC-051 as rewritten, which refuses earlier and more broadly.

criteria.requirement: No protected request is routed, performed, continued, fulfilled or emulated by Falcon unless its initiating frame is reference-identical to the main frame of the page under test. A request initiated by any other frame, including a frame whose own origin equals the top-level origin but whose ancestor chain does not, and including a same-origin nested frame, is refused before the route is armed and before any request is issued, with POLICY_PROTECTED_CROSS_ORIGIN_UNSUPPORTED exit 18 and the initiator origin audited alongside the top-level, approved and target origins. A request whose initiator cannot be established is refused before arming with POLICY_PROTECTED_INITIATOR_UNSUPPORTED exit 18: a service-worker-originated request, an initiator accessor that throws or yields a falsy, detached or unparsable frame, and a request from a popup or an opener; no such refusal is recoverable, retried or downgraded to a warning. The same initiator requirement is re-evaluated immediately before the hop-zero request and a failure there is labelled detection rather than prevention. Verification: a runtime case in the cross-origin-iframe topology asserting refusal before arming and zero POSTs at the target, whose inversion restores a top-level-only gate and must record a POST carrying the cookie the browser withheld; a nested-chain case; a worker-initiator case; an Origin-header cross-check case that also asserts an absent Origin header does not refuse; and a case detaching the initiator between arming and dispatch. The limitation text states that a protected action triggered from a same-origin nested frame is unavailable, and that on engines where the service-worker accessor is always null the reference-identity check is the only discriminator and blocked service workers remain mandatory. The criterion is retained unweakened as an entry requirement of 18P-PROTECTED-NONGET. Its refusal obligations are subsumed by AC-051 as rewritten, which refuses earlier and more broadly.
